servers.name: weave
servers.start_policy: start with the primary MCP client session; restart by restarting the client

servers.name: weave-session
servers.start_policy: start only for workflow lifecycle clients that need claim, guard, close, or handoff tools

servers.name: weave-lite
servers.start_policy: start only for constrained contexts that need minimal task tracking

servers.name: weave-inspect
servers.start_policy: start only for read-only research, review, audit, or quality inspection clients

all.purpose: Full backward-compatible MCP surface for general work
all.start_when: Use as the default server for general interactive work or when a client cannot select narrower scoped servers.

graph.purpose: Graph mutation surface for specialised planning/build agents
graph.start_when: Optional local server for agents that intentionally create, link, update, or delete graph nodes.

session.purpose: Workflow lifecycle surface for claim, guard, close, and session handoff
session.start_when: Use for agents whose primary job is claim, edit guard, close, recovery, or session handoff.

lite.purpose: Minimal task-tracking surface for constrained contexts
lite.start_when: Use where context budget is tight and only bootstrap/status/work/done/edit-guard basics are needed.

inspect.purpose: Read-only observation, search, health, and quality inspection surface
inspect.start_when: Use for research, review, audit, search, health, quality, and other read-only inspection workflows.

WV_PATH.description: Path to the wv CLI binary used by MCP-spawned subprocesses

WV_PROJECT_ROOT.description: Repository root passed to MCP-spawned wv commands

WV_AGENT_ID.description: Explicit Weave claim/provenance identity for MCP-spawned wv commands
WV_AGENT_ID.default: Auto-detected, but explicit identity is required by the shipped config contract

WV_ACTIVE.description: Active node id inherited by MCP tools

WV_MCP_CALL_LOG.description: JSONL sink for MCP response telemetry

WV_MCP_ALLOW_NETWORK.description: Allow MCP lifecycle tools to run GitHub/network sync directly when set to 1

WV_MCP_STARTUP_REPORT.description: Emit structured startup JSON to stderr when set to 1

WV_MCP_PATTERNS_LIST_BUDGET_MS.description: Shared timeout budget (ms) for one weave_quality_patterns list call, covering both its own primary invocation and its internal report call combined -- test-only, production deployments should not set this

startup_report.note: code and detail are null on a passing ("pass") report; on a reported failure code is one of error_codes below and detail is the human-readable message. startup_failure is a process-startup exit (stderr plus exit 1), not a health-check report, because no report can be emitted after an unexpected main() failure.

semantics.running: Exactly one matching process is visible for the scope.
semantics.stale: More than one matching process is visible for the scope; restart the client-managed servers.
semantics.unknown: No matching process is visible. Client-managed stdio servers may be idle, so absence is advisory rather than stale.

invalid_scope.meaning: The --scope value is not one of the supported scopes.
invalid_scope.remediation: Pass one of: graph, session, inspect, lite, all.

wv_not_found.meaning: The wv CLI binary could not be located on any known path.
wv_not_found.remediation: Set WV_PATH to the wv binary, or run ./install.sh so ~/.local/bin/wv exists.

bad_project_root.meaning: WV_PROJECT_ROOT/WV_PROJECT_DIR is set but does not exist or is not a directory.
bad_project_root.remediation: Point WV_PROJECT_ROOT at a valid repository checkout, or unset it to fall back to the process cwd.

startup_failure.meaning: An unexpected exception occurred during MCP server startup (e.g. stdio transport connect failure).
startup_failure.remediation: Check stderr for the underlying exception; retry, and file an issue if it recurs.

network_policy.github_sync: disabled unless WV_MCP_ALLOW_NETWORK=1; otherwise tools return a CLI fallback
